901.content: Role-based visibility, global error filtering, and actual channel routing in usage and audit logs.

909.content: This guide explains role-based visibility in Usage Logs and Audit Logs, and how to identify the channel that actually handled a request.

910.content: Super administrators can view complete logs for all users. In Usage Logs, choose Only Errors in the type filter to show error calls from every user. The filter keeps errors that occurred during retries, even when the final request succeeded.

911.content: The channel column identifies the channel that actually handled the request. When investigating routing, use the actual channel, model, status, and request ID in the log rather than relying only on the model name shown by the client.

912.content: Administrators can view only their own request, recharge, management-operation, and error-call logs. Username, role, and URL parameters cannot expand this scope. Administrators do not get a global Only Errors filter, but their own error records remain visible according to their permissions.

913.content: Regular users can view only their own request, recharge, and administrator-operation logs. They cannot view error logs or another user's logs.

914.content: Super administrators can view audit events for all users and filter by username. Administrators and regular users are restricted to audit events belonging to the currently authenticated account; page parameters cannot expand this server-side scope.

915.content: The audit event channel.status_update means channel status update. It records a manual status operation on one channel. The current code accepts an enabled or manually disabled target status; changed=false means the request succeeded but the channel state did not change. Batch operations use channel.status_update_batch. Check the event details, operator, and timestamp for the specific operation.

2706.content: Sample rate: samples per second, commonly 16kHz (sufficient for speech recognition) and 24kHz or 44.1kHz (higher fidelity). A mismatched sample rate causes pitch shifts on playback or lower transcription quality.

2707.content: Bit depth and channels: 16 bit mono is the common choice for speech; stereo and higher bit depths increase file size without the model necessarily using them.

2708.content: Container and codec: MP3 is lossy and small; WAV is usually uncompressed and large; PCM is raw samples without a container, so playback needs the sampling specification supplied manually.

2709.content: Duration and size: upload limits often constrain file size and duration together. Converting to a higher sample rate does not improve recognition accuracy, only makes limits easier to hit.

2710.content: Synchronous vs. streaming: TTS returns audio bytes and ASR returns JSON. Streaming reduces time to the first word or first segment without changing the total billed amount.

2745.content: HTTP streaming: one response delivers audio chunks or SSE events. It is not a bidirectional realtime session; do not JSON-parse binary audio.

2746.content: Asynchronous task: receive an ID, then query status. Video generation commonly uses this flow; ordinary TTS/ASR does not.

2747.content: Realtime: keep a session connected to send audio continuously, interrupt playback, and handle events. File upload is not a substitute.

3191.content: Three kinds of numbers come first; the parameters and prices below only make sense once they are separated:

3192.content: Pixel dimensions: the real width × height, such as 1024x1024. It sets the actual resolution of the file, not the file size, and it is not a quality tier.

3193.content: Aspect ratio: ratios such as 1:1, 16:9, and 9:16 only determine the shape of the frame. One ratio can map to several pixel dimensions; naming a ratio does not specify the output size.

3194.content: Resolution tier: tiers such as 1K, 2K, and 4K. Vendor-native tiers are defined by longest edge or product line, while this site's per-image billing tiers are classified by longest edge; the names match but the boundaries may not, so neither can be inferred from the other.

3195.content: There are also three common misconceptions: quality controls rendering quality, not compression quality; PNG, JPEG, and WebP are file formats, and renaming an extension does not convert one to another; Base64 and URL are delivery methods, not resolutions. See section 4 below, "Image specifications and billing", for the itemized comparison.

3930.content: Understand these terms first; every parameter below depends on them.

3931.content: Token: the smallest billing unit for text the model reads and writes. Roughly 4 English characters or 1 to 2 Chinese characters count as one token, depending on the model tokenizer. Input tokens and output tokens are priced separately.

3932.content: Context window: the combined input-plus-output token limit for one request. Longer history leaves less room for the answer; exceeding the limit can reject the request or truncate it and return finish_reason as length.

3933.content: Message role: system or developer sets behavioral boundaries, user is user input, assistant is model output, and tool returns a tool result. The order of roles is itself the conversation history.

3934.content: Stateless: the server does not store your conversation. Every request must resend the needed history, and longer history costs more.

3935.content: Streaming: the server returns increments over SSE so the client can render as it receives. It reduces time to first token, not total duration or cost, and it is not an asynchronous task.

3936.content: Tool calling: the model does not execute functions. It returns a structured call intent; your program executes it and sends the result back as a new message, and the model continues.

3951.content: More parameters is not better: temperature, top_p, reasoning_effort, and other sampling or reasoning parameters are supported to different degrees across models. The gateway passes them through to the channel; unsupported ones may error or be ignored. Send a minimal request first, then add parameters one at a time.

3961.content: Success is not "some data arrived". It means HTTP 2xx, a sensible final finish_reason, and complete concatenated text. If the stream breaks, finish with what you received rather than automatically resending the same paid request.

3962.content: Tool calling comes in two kinds, and mixing them up is a common source of bugs:

3963.content: Client-side functions (function calling): you declare the function signature, the model returns a call intent, your program executes it and returns the result. Both data and execution stay on your side.

3964.content: Server-side tools: executed on the model side, such as the built-in web search in Responses. You only see the final answer and citations, not the intermediate retrieval.

3966.content: Key points: arguments is a JSON string, not an object; the tool result must carry the matching tool_call_id; one turn may contain several tool calls, and parallel_tool_calls controls whether they are requested in parallel. Tool calling consumes extra tokens, and retries after errors may be billed again.

3967.content: Synchronous, non-streaming: the connection stays open until generation ends and returns one complete JSON body. Good for short replies and backend batch jobs.

3968.content: Streaming: the same request returns events incrementally over SSE. You must handle termination reasons and mid-stream breaks.

3969.content: Asynchronous background tasks: obtain a task or response ID, then collect the result via polling or a webhook. Native OpenAI Responses offers a background workflow, but this gateway has no matching retrieval or cancel endpoint, so do not simply add the background parameter.

3970.content: Parallel requests: the client sends several independent HTTP requests and handles success, rate limiting, and cost separately. n is the number of candidates, and parallel_tool_calls is multiple tool calls within one turn; neither equals HTTP concurrency.

3971.content: Ordinary message endpoints are stateless; send the needed history each time. Stateful response IDs are also subject to upstream routing and data retention limits. A vendor-direct connection must change both the vendor domain and the credentials; replacing only the model name is not enough.

4152.content:
What should I do about a 401 or Invalid token?
Check that the header is Authorization: Bearer <Key>, that the key belongs to this gateway and has not been revoked, and that you did not paste your login password or a provider key.

4153.content:
Why do I get 404 or a missing-model error?
model must be a full model ID from Models & pricing, and your key's group must be allowed to use it. SDK users should also confirm that baseURL includes /v1.

4154.content:
Should I retry a 429?
Read the response body first. For rate limiting, retry with exponential backoff and jitter; for exhausted quota or balance, retrying cannot succeed — top up or adjust the limit instead.

4155.content:
When is a streamed response complete?
Only after data: [DONE] and a final chunk carrying finish_reason. If the connection drops without an end marker, treat the reply as incomplete and do not automatically resend a request you have already paid for.

4156.content:
max_tokens or max_completion_tokens?
Use max_completion_tokens for Chat Completions. max_tokens is the legacy field and only some models still accept it. Never send both; /v1/completions still uses only max_tokens.

4157.content:
Why does temperature have no effect?
Some reasoning models fix sampling or accept only default values, and the gateway passes values through to the provider. Follow that model's documentation and errors instead of assuming every OpenAI parameter applies.

7217.content: Embeddings map text or other model-allowed inputs into fixed-length vectors for semantic retrieval, clustering, and similarity analysis. They do not return chat answers or directly execute searches; a retrieval pipeline usually has three stages: embedding recall of candidates, reranking for precision, and model generation of the answer. See OpenAI embeddings and Gemini embeddings for endpoint details.

7234.content: Dimensions: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small defaults to 1536 dimensions and text-embedding-3-large to 3072; Gemini Embedding 2 supports 128–3072 dimensions (recommended 768, 1536, or 3072), while gemini-embedding-001 defaults to 3072. Dimensions can be lowered within the model range but not raised above its limit; both vendors tie vector-store storage and retrieval cost directly to dimensions.

7235.content: Normalization and similarity: OpenAI returns unit-length vectors, so the dot product is cosine similarity; Gemini requires renormalization at dimensions other than 3072 (gemini-embedding-2 handles it automatically, while gemini-embedding-001 requires manual work). A vector store must fix one distance metric.

7236.content: Index and query must be homogeneous: the same document set and queries must use the same model, dimensions, and task configuration. After changing the model or dimensions, the old index and new vectors are not comparable and must be rebuilt.

7237.content: index is not a ranking: the index in the response only identifies which input the vector corresponds to, for alignment with the source text; relevance ranking is the job of reranking, see Reranking.

7238.content: Synchronous and batch: embeddings are synchronous requests with no SSE; large batches go through the Batch API or batchEmbedContents, not a forced loop of single calls.

8412.content: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio video generation protocol: Wan and HappyHorse share an asynchronous task endpoint; they differ in model ID, input structure, and aspect parameters.

8420.content: Wan and HappyHorse are both video generation model families on the Alibaba Cloud Model Studio platform, and they share the same DashScope asynchronous protocol: the submission endpoint, the X-DashScope-Async header, the task query path, the status strings, and the result fields are all identical. They differ in only three places — model ID, input structure, and aspect parameters.

8437.content: First-frame or reference image to video (HappyHorse)

8438.content: input.media containing first_frame or 1–9 reference_image images

8445.content: Task lifecycle: PENDING → RUNNING → SUCCEEDED, with FAILED as the failed terminal state, plus CANCELED and UNKNOWN. Only SUCCEEDED reads output.video_url.

8446.content: Two IDs have different roles: output.task_id is used to query the task; request_id only traces a single HTTP request. Keep both when troubleshooting.

8447.content: Polling rhythm: the official recommendation is to query every 15 seconds. Task IDs and result URLs are both valid for 24 hours; after expiry, a query returns UNKNOWN.

8448.content: Input structure differs by model family: Wan image-to-video uses input.img_url; HappyHorse uses the input.media array, whose elements carry type (first_frame or reference_image) and url. The two structures are not interchangeable.

8449.content: Aspect parameters differ by model family: Wan text-to-video uses parameters.size (宽*高, for example 1280*720), and Wan image-to-video uses parameters.resolution (480P, 720P, 1080P); HappyHorse text-to-video and reference-image-to-video use parameters.ratio (for example 16:9), while first-frame image-to-video follows the first-frame image.

8450.content: Audio only on some Wan generations: Wan2.6 and Wan2.5 generate music or sound effects that match the picture by default, and you can also supply WAV or MP3 through input.audio_url; Wan2.2 and Wan2.1 output silent video by default. The HappyHorse documentation has no audio input or output parameters.

8451.content: Billing is measured in output seconds: usage.duration in the query response is the output video duration. Unit prices, settlement of failed tasks, and refund rules follow the vendor's pricing page and billing.

8458.content: wan2.6-i2v, wan2.6-i2v-flash, wan2.5-i2v-preview, wan2.2-i2v-plus, wan2.2-i2v-flash, wan2.1-i2v-turbo, wan2.1-i2v-plus

8462.content: wan2.6-t2v is 2–15 seconds; wan2.5-t2v-preview is 5 or 10 seconds; wan2.2 and wan2.1 text-to-video is fixed at 5 seconds; wan2.1-i2v-turbo supports 3, 4, or 5 seconds

8464.content: Wan2.6 and Wan2.5 automatically generate music or sound effects; audio_url supports WAV and MP3, 3–30 seconds, up to 15 MB; Wan2.2 and Wan2.1 are silent by default

8466.content: Image-to-video uses input.img_url, supporting a public URL or Base64; image width and height are 240–8000 pixels, up to 20 MB for Wan2.6/2.5

8475.content: Text-to-video and reference-image-to-video: 16:9 (default), 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 4:5, 5:4, 9:21, 21:9; image-to-video follows the first frame and allows 1:2.5 to 2.5:1

8477.content: 3–15 seconds, default 5 seconds; this range is explicit in the happyhorse-1.0-t2v, image-to-video, and reference-image-to-video documentation, while the happyhorse-1.1-t2v documentation does not state a range

8479.content: Image-to-video takes 1 first frame with a shortest side of at least 300 pixels; reference-image-to-video takes 1–9 images with a shortest side of at least 400 pixels; up to 20 MB each; formats JPEG, JPG, PNG, WEBP

8481.content: watermark defaults to true, and when enabled shows HappyHorse in the bottom-right corner; seed ranges from 0 to 2147483647

8482.content: Wan's size is concrete pixels and resolution is a tier; the two serve different endpoints: 1080P portrait text-to-video must be written as 1080*1920, not 1080P; image-to-video is the reverse and accepts only 480P, 720P, 1080P. HappyHorse first-frame image-to-video does not read ratio; the output ratio is determined by the image. Wan2.2 and Wan2.1 text-to-video are fixed at 5 seconds, and a longer duration will not produce a longer clip. Wan2.6 and Wan2.5 always generate an audio track; when downstream does not need audio, remove it in post, or first confirm whether that model offers a disable parameter. When the number of reference images is 1–9, [Image N] in the prompt must match the order of media; a wrong order references the wrong image.

8515.content: Grok Imagine uses xAI's asynchronous video API: submit a task with POST /v1/videos/generations and get a request_id, then poll with GET /v1/videos/{request_id}. A text prompt generates a video directly; supplying image enters image-to-video, and supplying reference images or keyframes enters reference-to-video.

8536.content: Task lifecycle: query status has only pending, done, and failed. While pending, progress is 0–99; it is 100 when done, and may be omitted when failed.

8537.content: request_id is the polling identifier: it is not an idempotency key. After a submission timeout, do not conclude that the task was not created just because no response arrived; save and query the possible request_id first.

8538.content: Polling cadence: the official documentation does not specify a fixed interval. Clients can use 5–10 seconds and set an overall wait limit; stop immediately after failed.

8539.content: Duration and frame: duration ranges from 1–15 seconds, defaulting to 8 seconds; image-to-video ignores aspect_ratio, and the frame follows the input image. resolution defaults to 480p, and grok-imagine-video-1.5 supports native 1080p.

8540.content: Audio switch: the capability page lists generate_audio, default true; set it to false to request silence. The REST reference does not list the field separately, so actual availability depends on what the interface returns.

8541.content: Billing unit: usage.cost_in_usd_ticks in the query response is the cost counter for this task. The exact conversion, unit price, and failed-task settlement follow the vendor's pricing page.

8551.content: 1–15 seconds, default 8 seconds; editing an existing video does not accept a custom duration

8553.content: generate_audio defaults to true; false requests silence; follow the capability page description

8555.content: image first frame, reference_images reference images, keyframes up to 4, last_frame last frame (1.5)

8560.content: The default 480p suits previews, while 720p and 1080p increase generation time and cost. Image-to-video ignores aspect_ratio, and the frame is determined by image; to control landscape or portrait, handle it while preparing the input image. duration defaults to 8 seconds, and actual elapsed time also depends on queuing, so do not estimate from duration alone. generate_audio is described on the capability page but not listed separately in the REST reference; before integrating, verify with a short request whether the current model accepts the field.

8566.content: After done, download video.url; to write into your own object storage, you can also use output.upload_url or storage_options in the request. On failed, read error.code and error.message.

9792.content: Veo 3.1 video generation: predictLongRunning asynchronous operations, polling, and the 2026-10-22 retirement note.

9800.content: Veo generates video through a Gemini API long-running operation: call predictLongRunning to start a task, get the operation name, then poll that operation and download an MP4 from the file URI in the response when it completes.

9801.content: On the Gemini API, preview models such as veo-3.1-generate-preview and veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview were retired on 2026-10-22. This page keeps the protocol structure for understanding existing calls and as a migration reference; the endpoint is no longer usable as a production interface. Migrate to gemini-omni-1.2-flash, or use a GA model on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

9807.content: Prompt, first frame, last frame, or reference images

9818.content: An operation is not a task ID: the creation response returns name, for example models/veo-3.1-generate-preview/operations/.... Use this full name for polling, reading results, and troubleshooting.

9819.content: Completion requires done: true: done: false only means processing continues. With done: true, also check whether an error exists and whether response.generateVideoResponse.generatedSamples[0].video.uri is empty.

9820.content: Duration range: the vendor states at least 11 seconds and up to 6 minutes at peak. Poll at 10–15 second intervals and set a client-side overall wait limit.

9821.content: Duration and resolution are linked: duration has only three values, 4, 6, and 8 seconds. With 1080p, 4k, reference images, or video extension, duration must be 8 seconds; you cannot change a 4-second request directly to 1080p.

9822.content: Audio is generated with the model: the Gemini API documentation describes audio as always on, with no separate generateAudio switch. Prompts can include dialogue, sound effects, and ambient sound.

9823.content: Billing differs by platform: the Gemini API and the Agent Platform have separate billing and quota systems, and unit prices follow the vendor's pricing page. After the preview models were retired, new calls should no longer incur charges.

9828.content: veo-3.1-generate-preview, veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview, veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview; veo-3.0-generate-001, veo-3.0-fast-generate-001. The Gemini API documentation marks these IDs as Deprecated

9848.content: Resolution and duration are not independent options: 1080p, 4k, reference images, and extension all require 8 seconds; 4 or 6 seconds can only use 720p. At most 3 reference images are allowed, and the first and last frames constrain the picture rather than serving as style references. Audio is always generated and cannot be disabled through a parameter. After migrating to the Agent Platform, the model IDs, authentication, and quotas all change, so you cannot keep using this page's endpoint by simply swapping in a GA model name.

9849.content: Confirm the platform and credentials. The Gemini API uses x-goog-api-key; the Agent Platform uses its own authentication, and the two are not interchangeable.

9850.content: Submit to POST /v1beta/models/{MODEL_ID}:predictLongRunning with instances and parameters. Put the prompt in instances[0].prompt and the first frame in instances[0].image.

9851.content: Save the name from the response. A successful creation only means the operation was created, not that the video is downloadable.

9852.content: Poll GET /v1beta/{operation_name} until done: true. If an error exists, stop according to the error rather than continuing to wait.

9853.content: Read the download address from response.generateVideoResponse.generatedSamples[0].video.uri, request that URI with the API key, and allow HTTP redirects.

9854.content: Copy the file to your own storage. The official documentation says generated videos are retained for 2 days, and an extension reference resets the timer; do not rely on a long-lived vendor URL.

9855.content: The following archive illustration shows the payload structure of the original Gemini API. The preview models were retired on 2026-10-22, so it does not create new tasks today; the operation name and URL are illustrative values.

9859.content: If done: true but there are no generatedSamples or the URI is empty, treat it as a failure and keep the operation name.

9861.content: Auth header: x-goog-api-key: PASTE_API_KEY_HERE, sent together with Content-Type: application/json.

9862.content: Two addresses: direct Gemini API access uses https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta with the x-goog-api-key header; use https://api.dwchainless.com and Authorization: Bearer plus this site's key only when the channel explicitly confirms this gateway mapping; do not assume that replacing the address and authentication is sufficient. If SimiRouter provides a model with the same name, the path, fields, and polling method depend on the channel mapping. GA models on the Agent Platform use regional addresses such as https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com and project authentication; that is neither a generativelanguage address nor a model-string substitution.

9863.content: Timeout and idempotency: after a start-request timeout, first check whether an operation was created; saving name matters more than saving the HTTP status. Do not restart the same task just because the wait is long.

9864.content: Migration note: the interface shape of gemini-omni-1.2-flash differs from predictLongRunning, so existing polling code may have to be rewritten. Before migrating, rely on the official migration documentation and the model list available to your account.
